case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers a Bluetooth SIG qualification support engagement for a customer product using a prequalified Bluetooth module. The discussion includes qualification scope determination, reuse of Host and Controller subsystem QDIDs, RF/RF PHY test applicability, registration workflow management, and compliance documentation handling. The consultant also explains why the project requires Multi-Design qualification handling instead of a simpler single Component reuse path. Later in the thread, the customer asks whether changing BLE service UUIDs from SIG-defined 16-bit UUIDs to proprietary 128-bit UUIDs affects Bluetooth SIG qualification status.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The consultant determined that the referenced Bluetooth module was not a standalone Component registration but instead required separate Host and Controller subsystem QDID references. Because the referenced Controller subsystem supported BLE only, the final product qualification had to be registered as BLE-only rather than BR/EDR/BLE. The thread also discusses how the newer SIG consistency checks introduced after July 2024 increase validation complexity when combining multiple QDIDs, including possible ICS correction work and TCW handling during submission review. The consultant further explains that proprietary 128-bit UUID GATT services are treated as custom profiles outside SIG-defined profile specifications, so they do not require explicit declaration updates or additional SIG qualification actions.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant consistently bases decisions on the exact qualification structure and capabilities of the referenced Bluetooth declarations rather than on marketing descriptions or assumptions from the module vendor. If a product references separate Host and Controller subsystem QDIDs, it must be handled as a Multi-Design qualification with additional consistency validation requirements. Qualification scope must also remain aligned with the actual capabilities declared by the referenced subsystem QDIDs, meaning a BLE-only Controller cannot support BR/EDR qualification claims. For proprietary 128-bit UUID services, the consultant applies the principle that SIG qualification only formally governs SIG-defined profiles and specifications, leaving custom profile validation to the product implementer.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrectly treating a subsystem combination as a single Component registration could cause qualification inconsistencies, declaration errors, additional ICS correction work, and submission delays. Declaring unsupported BR/EDR capability for a BLE-only subsystem combination could trigger consistency check failures or rejection during SIG review. Misunderstanding RF reuse eligibility could lead either to unnecessary RF/RF PHY testing costs or to improper omission of required testing. Incorrectly assuming that proprietary 128-bit UUID changes require requalification could also result in unnecessary engineering effort, testing, or administrative work.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always validate the actual Bluetooth SIG qualification structure behind a module declaration instead of relying on vendor terminology alone. The qualification outcome depends on the precise combination of referenced QDIDs, subsystem capabilities, and SIG consistency rules. Multi-QDID reuse scenarios require careful verification of Host/Controller compatibility, qualification scope alignment, and consistency check behavior. Proprietary GATT services using 128-bit UUIDs generally remain outside formal SIG profile qualification scope, so implementation responsibility stays with the product manufacturer.
